note: Metadata only: the clips are never committed (several have no licence). Fetch them locally with battlefield.sh. Splits were fixed on 2026-10-10 before any detector work: tune on 'dev' only, run 'heldout' once with frozen parameters. Never commit or publish frames of these clips; report numbers only.

clips.camera: moving: drone tracks backward along the road, starting near-nadir and rotating/pulling out to a high oblique
clips.content: Autumn daylight, low sun with long shadows. A military convoy of about 4-5 vehicles (wheeled armoured personnel carriers or IFVs, a military truck and light vehicles) drives along a straight dirt road cut through pine and birch forest, with parallel sandy tracks and a lake coming into view. Targets start medium-sized and shrink to small as the drone climbs and the view rotates about 45 degrees. No people visible on foot.
clips.caveats: Same stock provider as amad-test2. Short (15.8 s). Low resolution (596x336).

clips.camera: high oblique from long stand-off, slow forward drift and pan (near-hover)
clips.content: Overcast daylight over an arid, hilly military training range with marked plots, scrub and a mountain ridge behind. A column of roughly 6-10 military vehicles (trucks and tracked or wheeled armour) moves along a dirt road beside the range, with more vehicles staged near structures in the middle distance. All targets are small (tens of pixels) against low-contrast brown terrain. Different scene, terrain and altitude from amad-test1.
clips.caveats: Same stock provider as dev clip amad-test1 (different scene). Short (11.4 s). Low resolution (596x336).

clips.original_source: unstated; burned-in 'WORLD MILITARY' logo suggests a YouTube military-compilation channel
clips.overlay_notes: 'WORLD MILITARY' channel logo bottom-left and a small 'illustration' tag top-right; no boxes.
clips.camera: moving: low-altitude oblique drone flying forward along the beach
clips.content: Bright daylight on a sandy beach. About 5 tracked amphibious assault vehicles drive in loose file along the waterline, leaving track marks, with surf on the right and vegetation on the left. The vehicles grow from small to large as the drone advances; the nearest passes close under the camera at the end. No people on foot.
clips.caveats: Only 6.1 s, below the 10 s target; kept because it is a rare real drone-view military clip from a different source.

clips.original_source: SYNTHETIC: ARMA 3 game footage captured by the repo author (devlog https://youtu.be/DKLcZ7jMpyU, YouTube is blocked here). This is a detector-output GIF.
clips.overlay_notes: Red/orange detector boxes with class labels ('CSAT Marid', 'CSAT Varsuk' + confidence) from the author's YOLOv5, plus game UAV HUD text (SPD/ALT AGL ~102 m, grid, UTC time) and a centre reticle.
clips.camera: hover: fixed oblique view at ~100 m AGL (per HUD), essentially static
clips.content: Simulated (ARMA 3) Mediterranean scrubland with a dirt road, trees and two buildings. One armoured vehicle drives down the road and across the field toward the centre reticle, sometimes accompanied by a second vehicle at the top edge. Encoded from a 5 fps GIF.
clips.caveats: Synthetic, with burned-in boxes from someone else's detector, so it contaminates any detection metric. Use only as a pipeline smoke test. Never score on it.

clips.repo: MEVA public S3 bucket s3://mevadata-public-01 (Kitware / IARPA DIVA; mevadata.org)
clips.original_source: MEVA dataset UAV drop 01: DJI Inspire 1 v2 with Zenmuse X3, 3840x2160@30, recorded 2018-03-07 at the Muscatatuck Urban Training Center (Indiana National Guard urban training site); recompressed by Kitware (crf 26)
clips.camera: moving: oblique drone translating and slowly rotating over the training town at roughly 30-60 m
clips.content: Overcast late-winter daylight over the MUTC mock town: flat-roofed school and institutional buildings, a parking area, roads and bare trees. Static military display pieces stand on a plinth by a stone tower (a desert-camouflage tank and a second tan armoured vehicle) among parked civilian cars, a small UTV, and an occasional moving car. Very few or no pedestrians. Tests static armour versus civilian vehicles, strong parallax and building occlusion. Downscaled from 4K to 1920x1080.
clips.caveats: Training-town scene with civilian vehicles and display armour, not a live exercise. MEVA has activity annotations for its ground cameras (not downloaded).

clips.original_source: HIT-UAV dataset, Suo et al., 'HIT-UAV: A high-altitude infrared thermal dataset for UAV-based object detection', Scientific Data 10:227 (2023); recorded by the authors. Filename encodes flight altitude (m) and camera angle (deg; 90 = nadir).
clips.camera: oblique (~30 deg setting) at ~60 m, slow translation and pan along the stands
clips.content: Thermal view of a sports ground: running track, artificial-turf field, spectator stands and a tree-lined walkway. Dozens of pedestrians walk singly and in small groups on the track, walkway and field. People are small warm blobs about 5-15 px tall, with frequent close passes that stress the tracker. No vehicles of note. 7.5 fps.
clips.caveats: Civilian scene (not military). HIT-UAV's 2,898 labelled images were extracted from the same flight campaign, so any detector pre-trained on HIT-UAV may already have seen near-identical frames. Only the raw sample videos were downloaded; no labels.

clips.original_source: HIT-UAV dataset, Suo et al., 'HIT-UAV: A high-altitude infrared thermal dataset for UAV-based object detection', Scientific Data 10:227 (2023); recorded by the authors. Filename encodes flight altitude (m) and camera angle (deg; 90 = nadir).
clips.camera: moving: oblique (~30 deg setting) at ~120 m, flying along a curved road
clips.content: Thermal view of a campus or suburban road with flat-roofed buildings, lawns and parking lots. Small moving and parked cars, a few pedestrians, and a long dark vehicle (bus or truck) near the end. Targets are very small at this altitude, and the strong forward motion makes it a good small-object test with ego-motion. Different scene and altitude from the dev thermal clip. 7.5 fps.
clips.caveats: Civilian scene (not military). HIT-UAV's 2,898 labelled images were extracted from the same flight campaign, so any detector pre-trained on HIT-UAV may already have seen near-identical frames. Only the raw sample videos were downloaded; no labels.

clips.original_source: HIT-UAV dataset, Suo et al., 'HIT-UAV: A high-altitude infrared thermal dataset for UAV-based object detection', Scientific Data 10:227 (2023); recorded by the authors. Filename encodes flight altitude (m) and camera angle (deg; 90 = nadir).
clips.camera: nadir (90 deg) at ~70 m, slow drift with slight rotation
clips.content: Top-down thermal view of a paved plaza beside a tree-lined path, with steps, a bench and a lamp post. A tight file of about 4 pedestrians walks along the path, while scattered individuals and pairs cross the plaza. A useful nadir person-detection and grouping case, the closest analogue here to a dismounted patrol seen from overhead. 7.5 fps.
clips.caveats: Civilian scene (not military). HIT-UAV's 2,898 labelled images were extracted from the same flight campaign, so any detector pre-trained on HIT-UAV may already have seen near-identical frames. Only the raw sample videos were downloaded; no labels.
